subject.title: [Feature]: Add global --dry-run mode to prevent all tool calls from executing

question: Should OpenClaw add a core run-scoped dry-run/plan mode for agent tool execution, and if so should it be CLI-only first or a canonical Gateway plus embedded execution contract?
rationale: The source shows the feature is still missing, but the correct shape affects the core tool execution boundary, hook ordering, provider/client-tool parity, and whether users can trust dry-run as a safety control.

options.title: Design canonical run-scoped preview mode
options.body: Define a run-context dry-run/plan contract across Gateway and embedded paths, with redaction and tests for built-in, plugin, client, and deferred tools before implementation.

options.title: Keep as CLI-only experiment
options.body: Allow a narrow `openclaw agent --local --dry-run` prototype while explicitly documenting that Gateway and client tools are out of scope.

options.title: Defer to broader safe modes
options.body: Keep this issue open as input for the broader Ask/Plan/Modify workflow discussion instead of adding a separate dry-run flag now.

recommendation.title: Design canonical run-scoped preview mode
recommendation.body: Define a run-context dry-run/plan contract across Gateway and embedded paths, with redaction and tests for built-in, plugin, client, and deferred tools before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: Current main history and recent related agent tool-definition work make this the best available routing candidate for the execution-path decision.
